test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question:
Given below are six sentences of a paragraph. Sentence A is the beginning whereas sentence F is the last sentence of the para. The middle four sentences are jumbled up. Select the option that gives their correct order forming a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The first hour passed off quietly.

B. In the second, they had Arithmetic.

C. Swaminathan was terribly bored.

D. Vedanayagam went out and returned in a fewminutes in the role of an Arithmetic teacher.

E. He droned on monotonously.

F. His teacher’s voice was beginning to get on his nerves.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph starts with an introduction of the situation, which is provided by **sentence A**: **"The first hour passed off quietly."**
 
• Next, **sentence B **logically follows as it introduces the subject of the second hour: "In the second, they had Arithmetic."
 
• Then, **sentence D** follows as it introduces Vedanayagam taking on the role of the Arithmetic teacher: "Vedanayagam went out and returned in a few minutes in the role of an Arithmetic teacher."
 
• **Sentence E** comes next as it describes Vedanayagam's teaching style: "He droned on monotonously."
 
• **Sentence C** follows as it indicates Swaminathan's reaction to the monotonous teaching: "Swaminathan was terribly bored."
 
• Finally, the paragraph concludes with** sentence F**: "His teacher’s voice was beginning to get on his nerves."

Hence, the correct Order of the sentence is = **A, B, D, E, C, F. (BDEC)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When arranging sentences to form a coherent paragraph, look for logical and chronological clues within the sentences.
 
• Pay attention to pronouns and definite articles, as they often refer back to something mentioned in a previous sentence.
